The eastern beaches

Event Planners in Randwick

Randwick City holds the coast from Coogee down to La Perouse, a racecourse in the middle and a university on its western edge. Those three things fill the calendar and fight over the same weekends. Send one brief and hear from planners who work the eastern beaches.

Coast rules apply hereReserves and clifftops are council land, and they stay public.
Get event planning quotesHow planning works
  • Coogee to La PerouseThe council area covers most of Sydney's eastern beaches.
  • Light rail from the cityLines now run to Randwick and to Kingsford from the CBD.
  • Carnival weeks are tightRacing dates fill accommodation and put traffic through the middle.

You can book the reserve. You cannot book the people walking through it.

Every clifftop and beach reserve between Coogee and Little Bay is public land with a permit system attached. You get a time slot and a chair limit, not the coastline to yourself.

Randwick City runs from Kensington and Kingsford across to the beaches at Coogee, Clovelly and Maroubra, then south along the coast to Malabar, Little Bay and La Perouse. Three institutions sit inside it and shape the calendar: Royal Randwick racecourse, the university at Kensington and the hospital campus beside it. Between them they produce graduations, conferences, industry dinners and race days, which is why event planners in Randwick work around a busier fixed calendar than most Sydney markets.

The coast is the drawcard and the complication. Clifftop reserves, beach parks and headlands here are council land, open to the public and available to you only with a permit. A southerly change in spring can arrive in twenty minutes, so a wet weather position is not a formality on this side of the city.

In and around Randwick

What are you planning in Randwick?

Six briefs dominate here, and two calendars sit underneath them: the racing calendar, which takes rooms and roads, and the academic year, which fills the western half of the council area.

Start with

Weddings

Ceremony on a clifftop reserve above Coogee or Clovelly, reception in a room with the ocean in it. The permit is the first job, the wind is the second, and the third is accepting that the coastal walk stays open and strangers will be in the background.

Parties and milestones

Beachfront rooms at Coogee and Maroubra carry most of the milestone birthdays here, and they book out from October. Anything on the sand or in a park needs a council booking, and alcohol rules in coastal reserves are stricter than people expect.

Find planners

Corporate events

The university and hospital campuses at Kensington and Randwick generate a year round run of conferences, symposia, graduations and industry dinners, most of them weekday and many of them with an academic timetable behind them. Health, research and education briefs dominate rather than finance.

Find planners

Engagement parties

Late afternoon at Clovelly or Little Bay, sixty to a hundred people, and the light doing the work. The catch is the southerly. Spring changes arrive fast on this coast, so the plan needs a covered position that is booked rather than hoped for.

Find planners

Proposals

The coastal walk between Coogee and Clovelly, the headland at Malabar and the rocks around La Perouse are the requests that come up most. All are public and busy at sunrise and sunset. A planner books the permit where one is needed and manages the timing and the getaway.

Private celebrations

Christenings, farewells, anniversaries and community events run through the halls, clubs and surf clubs from Kensington to Matraville. Many are booked inside two months, which suits a coordinator holding the caterer, the hire and the council booking to one timeline.

Planning support

How much help do you want in Randwick?

Anything with a permit and a weather risk benefits from more help than you think. A room booking at Coogee can run on coordination. A clifftop ceremony with a hundred guests and a wet weather site needs planning from the start.

Full planning

A planner carries the whole build with you, from the first budget conversation to the last supplier leaving.

Usually engaged nine to fourteen months out.

  • Venue and supplier shortlists
  • Contracts and payment schedule
  • Run sheet and floor plan
  • On the day, start to finish

You have made a start. A planner picks up the parts that have stalled and brings the rest into one plan.

Your plan is built. A coordinator takes it over in the final weeks and runs the day so you can be in it.

Usually engaged four to eight weeks out.

Venue sourcing

Planners who know a market can shortlist against your date, your numbers and your budget rather than sending you back to the same search results.

Event coordination

Coordination is the execution layer: suppliers confirmed, a run sheet everyone has, and one person answering questions on the day.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Randwick

Two of these questions are about the coast and two are about the calendar. Together they will tell you whether a planner has actually run events on this side of the city.

No. 01

Ask who lodges the reserve booking and when

Clifftops, beach reserves and parks across Randwick City are council land, and a ceremony with chairs or an arbour needs a booking well ahead of the date. Ask who applies, what the lead time is, how many guests the permit allows, and what the approved wet weather alternative is. A permit approved for a sunny reserve does not transfer to a hall in the rain.

No. 02

Ask them to check your date against the racing calendar

Race days at Randwick change the whole area for a weekend: accommodation goes, traffic thickens around Alison Road and Anzac Parade, and rideshare pricing climbs. Carnival weeks in autumn and spring are the ones to watch. Ask a planner to check your date before you commit, particularly if guests are travelling in and need somewhere to stay.

No. 03

Ask what the southerly plan is

This coast is exposed and spring changes come through fast, sometimes within half an hour. A good answer is specific: a covered position identified and booked, a call time for the decision, weighted styling rather than light, and a plan for moving a hundred chairs quickly. Vague reassurance about a marquee on standby is not a plan.

No. 04

Ask how guests arrive now the light rail runs

Light rail from the city to Randwick and Kingsford changed guest transport here for the better, and a planner should be using it. Ask which stop is closest to your venue, how long the walk is, and what the last service time is on your night. For anything at Malabar, Little Bay or La Perouse, the answer is buses or a coach, and that needs booking.

The coastal walk does not close for your ceremony. Plan the photographs around that, not against it.

On the ground

Sharing the coast with everyone else who turned up

Three things separate an event in Randwick City from one anywhere else in Sydney: the coast is public, the racecourse owns certain weekends, and the weather changes faster than the run sheet allows for.

A permit buys a slot, not the place

Council land is the default along this coast, and that shapes what a ceremony can actually be. The reserves above Coogee and Clovelly, the headlands at Malabar and Little Bay and the parks behind Maroubra all require a booking for chairs, an arbour, a signing table or amplified sound, with a fee, a capped guest number and a fixed time window. What the permit does not buy is exclusivity. The coastal walk stays open, swimmers keep crossing the grass, and a running group will come through at exactly the wrong moment. Plan the ceremony to work with that.

Race days take the beds and the roads

Royal Randwick sits in the middle of the council area, and its carnival dates ripple outwards. On a major race day, accommodation across the eastern suburbs is taken, traffic on Alison Road and Anzac Parade slows to a crawl in the afternoon, rideshare surges and parking near the course disappears. If your guest list includes people flying in, check the racing calendar before you check anything else. The autumn and spring carnival weeks are the ones that cost you options.

Weather, transport and the edges of the map

Two practical notes and one boundary worth knowing.

  • Southerly changes: spring afternoons on this coast can turn in half an hour, so book a covered position rather than relying on a forecast.
  • Light rail: services now run from the city to Randwick and to Kingsford, which handles the northern and western half of the council area well.
  • The southern end: Malabar, Little Bay and La Perouse have no light rail, so guests come by bus, car or coach.
  • Neighbouring councils: Bondi Junction and Double Bay sit in Waverley and Woollahra, not Randwick City.

Questions

Planning an event in Randwick

How much should I set aside for an event planner in Randwick?

Set the budget against scope, since planners quote a flat fee, an hourly rate or a share of total spend rather than a suburb rate. Two Randwick specific costs are worth allowing for separately: the council permit and booking fees for any reserve or beach park, and a wet weather contingency, because a covered fallback on this coast has to be booked rather than improvised. Ask for both as visible lines.

Do race days at Randwick affect my event?

They affect accommodation, traffic and transport pricing across the whole eastern suburbs. Royal Randwick sits inside this council area, and on a carnival weekend rooms are taken, Alison Road and Anzac Parade slow badly through the afternoon, and rideshare costs jump. If guests are travelling in and need somewhere to stay, check the racing calendar before you sign a venue contract, particularly for autumn and spring dates.

Can I get married on a Coogee or Clovelly clifftop?

Yes, with a council booking, and it is worth applying early for the popular reserves. The council manages the clifftops, beach parks and headlands across Randwick City, and a booking covers chairs, an arbour, a signing table and sometimes amplified sound, with a guest cap and a set time slot. The space stays public throughout. Ask your planner to secure an approved wet weather site at the same time, not later.

How do guests get to the eastern beaches now?

Light rail from the city reaches Randwick and Kingsford, which covers the northern and western half of the council area and removed a long standing transport headache. Coogee, Clovelly and Maroubra are a short bus ride or walk from those lines. The southern suburbs are different: Malabar, Little Bay and La Perouse have no light rail, so plan buses or book a coach, and check the last service time for your finish.

Is Bondi Junction part of Randwick?

No. Bondi Junction sits in the Waverley council area and Double Bay in Woollahra, both neighbouring Randwick City rather than inside it. It matters for permits, because a ceremony at a Bondi or Bronte reserve goes through a different council with its own fees, lead times and conditions. Most planners working the eastern suburbs cover all three areas, so ask which councils they have lodged applications with recently.

What is the best season for an outdoor event on this coast?

February to April is the most reliable window, with warm water, settled afternoons and light that holds later. Spring looks tempting and carries the southerly risk: a change can arrive within half an hour and take an unweighted ceremony with it. Winter is clear but cold and exposed on the clifftops. If you want an October or November date, book the covered fallback at the same time as the reserve.
